summary: All five criteria are evidenced and all five declared falsifications land. I applied each falsified_by mutation in a scratch copy, diffed to prove it landed, and in every case the row the field names went red: AC1 (required-field loop deleted, 10 rows red including 'a release declaring NO MEMBERS is refused'), AC2 (id_paths accumulation replaced with out[aid] = [Path(p)], the both-filenames row red), AC3 (member-kind whitelist deleted, the kind-spec row red), AC4 (member_digest returns plan_hash of the parsed front matter, the one-byte-below-front-matter negative control red), AC5 (member scan refuses instead of noticing, the zero-errors-one-notice row red). I also USED the feature: declaring this repository's first real release (releases/REL-0001, member PLAN-0018) leaves the FULL suite at 4530 passed 0 failed, identical to baseline, and a deliberately broken second release makes python3 .veldo/validate.py all exit 1 naming every cause, so the gate wiring has live teeth and no assertion pins today's empty release corpus. On the two questions I was asked to judge: (1) human_approval required at standard risk is NOT a contract violation - docs/setup.md:117 makes risk a declared floor that policy may raise and nothing may lower, and the only consumer (executor.merge_ready) treats required as strictly more conservative, so neither the spec nor .veldo/policy.yaml is wrong; the real defect is that the declaration is unsatisfied and unenforced (no approval artifact for VELDO-0011, while VELDO-0012 which declares the same field carries proof/VELDO-0012/approval-dmitry.json). (2) The FILE BYTES claim is true of member_digest (sha256 of read_bytes, all 64 hex, recorded on each resolved member, None when absent) but the word BOUND overreaches: no value is stored and nothing re-checks it, so a member is DIGESTED by its bytes today, not bound by them. Four real defects sit beside the criteria: two refusal messages that state something false, one live-corpus lower bound that reds after the migration this item's own notice exists to cause, and one confident zero in the stood-down report.

criteria.note: Drove the declared falsification: deleted the REQUIRED_FIELDS loop in record_problems (.veldo/release_contract.py:326-329), proved it landed with git diff, and the suite went 91 passed 13 failed - including the row the field names, 'a release declaring NO MEMBERS is refused, with the field named on the page a reader sees'. Verified the anti-vacuity legs independently: the table has 15 rows, the count assertion is bound to len(_RC_BAD) AND to a >= 15 floor so emptying it reds, the positive control requires the well-formed fixture to be accepted with zero errors and empty output, and the approval refusal is compared against the plan validator's OWN printed output rather than a hand-copied sentence. Verified every path citation in the criterion by reading the lines: validate.parse_yamlish at .veldo/validate.py:351, the plan approval refusal at .veldo/validate.py:500-503, PLAN_KINDS at :38. Two notes. (a) The parenthetical 'the ONE parser the whole repository reads front matter with' is false - validate.front_matter (.veldo/validate.py:47-59) is a second, cruder front-matter reader used for SPEC front matter in run_all (:846, :853), by scripts/update_index.py:39,104 and by five other organs; the substantive half, that this module adds no second YAML reader, does hold. Filed as F7. (b) CAUSE_MEMBER_SHAPE is declared, reachable and correct (I drove it: a member declaring kind with no target yields 'member 1 declares no target') but no assertion in the suite names it, so one of the seventeen declared causes is untested.

Drove the CORRECTED falsification the field names: replaced out.setdefault(aid, []).append(Path(p)) with out[aid] = [Path(p)] in id_paths, proved it landed, and the suite went 98 passed 6 failed with the named row red ('two plan files declaring PLAN-9999 are refused, and the refusal names BOTH files'). I independently checked the correction's own claims and they are all true: .veldo/validate.py:669 IS the bare reg[fm['id']] = {...} assignment, and git show d449286 -- .veldo/validate.py proves plan_registry is byte-unchanged by this item (validate.py gained exactly the two registration lines and nothing else), so 'the registry's return shape and contract do not move' is verified against the diff, not just asserted. Verified all seven named callers at their exact cited lines (.veldo/plan.py:49, budget.py:288, toe_budget.py:904, runstatus.py:136, judgment_load.py:581, intent_corpus.py:552, scripts/update_index.py:48). Re-measured the live corpus: 18 plan files, 18 distinct ids, plan_duplicate_ids == [], matching the spec's recorded 2026-08-11 reading. One nit: the criterion says the live read asserts ONLY the count equality, but scripts/suites/18_veldo_0011_release_contract.py:381-382 also asserts plan_duplicate_ids == []; it is implied by the equality so it adds no new pin, but it is more than the criterion claims.

Drove the declared falsification: deleted the 'if shape is None' member-kind whitelist test, proved it landed, and the named row went red ('a member declaring kind spec with target VELDO-0011 is refused') - the target-shape test does not cover for it, exactly as the criterion says the type rule is the load-bearing leg. Verified the rest by running the suite and by driving the module directly: the depth rows validate 3-level AND 5-level chains ending at a plan with releases == members == members_resolved == depth and no depth constant exists in the source; the cycle refusal names the ring in order (REL-9501 -> REL-9502 -> REL-9501) and a self-listing release is named as a ring of one; single parentage refuses with both releases named (I confirmed this over the LIVE corpus too: 'PLAN-0018 is claimed as a member by 2 releases: REL-0001, REL-0002'); every graph refusal has a one-member-different positive control that validates with zero errors. TWO DEFECTS in adjacent cases, both executed, filed as F1 and F2: a member whose target is a real PLAN or REL id is refused with the message 'which is a spec id: a spec binds to a plan and never to a release' because SPEC_ID_RE is a superset of both vocabularies, and a release declaring the SAME member twice draws a second, false refusal saying that member is 'claimed as a member by 2 releases: REL-1, REL-1'. The criterion's literal claims all hold; these are over-reach, and the suite drives both fixtures while asserting only the cause name, never the sentence, so neither is visible to the gate.

Drove the declared falsification: rewrote member_digest to load .veldo/plan.py and .veldo/validate.py and return plan_hash of the parsed front matter, proved it landed, and the suite went 100 passed 4 failed with the negative control red ('a ONE-BYTE edit BELOW the front matter changes the member digest while plan_hash over the same two files stays EQUAL') plus the width rows. Verified the properties independently: member_digest == hashlib.sha256(read_bytes()).hexdigest(), 64 lowercase hex, None (never '') for an unreadable file, recorded on each resolved member of release_report beside its target and path, digest_coverage = resolved/declared and None when nothing is declared - I read a live example: PLAN-0018 digests to 4f9a715a...cf3c0 with coverage 1.0. Verified plan_hash is untouched at .veldo/plan.py:216-222 and its shipped pin is real at scripts/suites/01_warp_0101_reviewer_notes.py:471. Verified engine/.veldo/release_contract.py and engine/releases/TEMPLATE.md are byte-identical to their live twins, and that engine/** is in publish.py's INCLUDE so a composed pack really does carry both. ONE overclaim, filed as F8: nothing in this item STORES or RE-CHECKS the digest - release_report recomputes it on every call and compares it to nothing - so today a member is digested by its bytes, not bound by them. The spec's own Out of scope block says so honestly, but .veldo/capabilities.yaml:181 says 'a plan body rewritten after the binding no longer matches', which asserts a binding that does not exist yet.

Drove the declared falsification: made the member scan append a CAUSE_BAD_KIND problem for a member plan declaring kind mvp and stopped appending the notice, proved it landed, and the named row went red ('a release whose member plan declares kind mvp validates with ZERO errors and exactly ONE notice'). Verified the rest by running: both stand-down conditions produce identical reports differing only in the naming field, both carry the full REPORT_KEYS shape a live read carries, the stand-down is keyed on the CANDIDATE FILE SET (a release file declaring no id is refused rather than standing the check down - I confirmed that row and the source), the template creates the directory and the check still stands down, a populated corpus does NOT stand down, check_plan_ids does not stand down with it, the notice fires only when a member plan declares kind mvp and not for its sibling fixture, and two mvp releases ARE refused with both named. Re-measured the rationale: 17 of 18 plan files declare kind mvp, the exception is plans/PLAN-0002-companion-home.md, exactly as recorded. TWO DEFECTS filed as F3 and F4. F3 is executed: the AC5 LIVE row's condition is kinds.count('mvp') > 1, a lower bound on a live set this item's own notice exists to shrink; I migrated 16 of the 17 plan files to kind: iteration in a scratch copy and that exact row went red, and its own label reads 'the count is read, not pinned'. F4 is executed: a stood-down release_report prints duplicate_ids {'release': [], 'plan': []} without ever reading the plan corpus, so with a real duplicate plan id present and no releases directory the report states a false empty while check_plan_ids correctly refuses it.

findings.text: member_claims accumulates one entry per member ENTRY rather than per release, so a release that declares the same member twice draws a SECOND, factually false refusal claiming the member has two parents. A release with members [plan PLAN-9101, plan PLAN-9101] is refused twice: correctly with member_declared_twice, and then with member_claimed_by_two_releases saying 'PLAN-9101 is claimed as a member by 2 releases: REL-1, REL-1'. There is one release, and it is named twice. AC3 promises this refusal names 'both releases'; here it names one release twice and states a wrong count, and the error total for one authoring mistake is 2. The suite drives exactly this fixture (scripts/suites/18_veldo_0011_release_contract.py:521-529) but asserts the cause with `in`, so the extra false problem is invisible to the gate. Fix: build claims from the set of distinct targets per release, in member_claims (.veldo/release_contract.py:467-476).
findings.evidence: Driven directly against the shipped module in /tmp/.../rev-VELDO-0011: RC.release_problems over a release declaring PLAN-9101 twice printed '[member_declared_twice] member 2 repeats target PLAN-9101, already declared as member 1' AND '[member_claimed_by_two_releases] PLAN-9101 is claimed as a member by 2 releases: REL-1, REL-1. A member has one parent or the group is not a forest'; RC.member_claims returned {'PLAN-9101': ['REL-1', 'REL-1']}.

findings.text: SPEC_ID_RE ([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*-\d+) is a superset of both member vocabularies, so the 'is a spec id' branch in record_problems (.veldo/release_contract.py:387-391) fires for targets that are plainly NOT spec ids. A member declaring kind release with target PLAN-9101 is refused with 'targets PLAN-9101, which is a spec id: a spec binds to a plan and never to a release, and the plan contract already types that id shape', and a member declaring kind plan with target REL-9309 gets the same sentence about REL-9309. These are the two most likely author mistakes in this contract (swapping kind and target between the two levels), and in both the refusal misnames the id's type and then explains a rule that does not apply. The generic else branch ('which is not a PLAN-\d+ id') is only reachable for a target that matches no PREFIX-digits shape at all. This contradicts the spec's error_taxonomy ('The causes are distinct rather than one undifferentiated invalid-release line') and its observability promise ('an author reads one line and knows which member to fix'). The suite drives both cases at scripts/suites/18_veldo_0011_release_contract.py:425-433 but asserts only the CAUSE, never the message, so the wrong sentence cannot red the gate. Fix: test the target against the OTHER member id shapes first and name the artifact type it actually is, and reach the spec-id sentence only when no member shape matches.
findings.evidence: Driven directly against the shipped module: RC.release_problems over a release with member (kind release, target PLAN-9101) printed 'member 1 (kind release) targets PLAN-9101, which is a spec id: a spec binds to a plan and never to a release...'; the same for (kind plan, target REL-9309). A target of 'not_an_id' produced the correct generic message, showing the else branch is only reachable for non-id text.

findings.text: The AC5 LIVE row asserts kinds.count('mvp') > 1 over this repository's live plan corpus (scripts/suites/18_veldo_0011_release_contract.py:794-796). That is a lower bound on a live set that THIS ITEM'S OWN NOTICE exists to drive to zero: the notice tells authors the plan-level kind mvp is legacy and should move to the release level, and the moment fewer than two plan files declare it the row reds. Its own label says 'the count is read, not pinned', which contradicts the condition. This is PLAN-0018 finding 26 ('THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING OF THE DAY'), which AC5 quotes, in the mirror direction, and the spec's own instruction to the implementing agent says every live read must be 'a READING of the corpus rather than a requirement that the corpus stay as it is today'. scripts/check_first_use.py cannot see it: its MUTATIONS table has one family (spend_recorded) and its docstring says a new corpus needs a new entry, and there is no sanctioned writer for a plan's kind. The same shape, weaker, sits at line 386: len(files) > 10. Fix: branch on what was measured - assert the notice discriminates when the corpus still carries the legacy kind, and assert it fires on nothing when the migration is complete.
findings.evidence: In /tmp/.../scratchpad/use-feature I migrated 16 of the 17 plan files from 'kind: mvp' to 'kind: iteration' (leaving one, the end state the notice pressures for) and ran python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 18_veldo_0011_release_contract: 103 passed, 1 failed, the single failure being 'SELFTEST FAIL: VELDO-0011 AC5 LIVE: the plan corpus really does declare the legacy kind mvp ... the count is read, not pinned'. Baseline in the same tree (release declared, plans untouched) was the full suite at 4530 passed 0 failed.

findings.text: A CONFIDENT ZERO in the stood-down report. _stood_down (.veldo/release_contract.py:586-593) returns duplicate_ids {'release': [], 'plan': []} as constants, but the plan half is a reading of a DIFFERENT corpus that the stand-down never performs. So when releases/ is absent or holds only the template, release_report states that the plan corpus carries no duplicate ids no matter what it carries. Every other zero in that report (releases, members, members_resolved) is genuinely true; this is the one cross-corpus figure and it can be false. The spec's own observability block forbids exactly this: 'A figure with no basis is not printed: an unresolved member carries digest None rather than an empty string, exactly as the estimation layer prints None rather than a confident zero.' The gate is unaffected because check_plan_ids is registered separately and still refuses, so this is a defect in the reporting surface, not in enforcement. Fix: either compute the plan half in the stood-down branch (it needs no releases) or carry None for it.
findings.evidence: Ran against the shipped module with two plan files both declaring PLAN-7001 and no releases directory: release_report returned stood_down True, stand_down 'no releases directory at all', duplicate_ids {'release': [], 'plan': []}, while RC.plan_duplicate_ids returned [('PLAN-7001', ['PLAN-7001-a.md', 'PLAN-7001-b.md'])] and check_plan_ids returned 1. Identical with a releases directory holding only TEMPLATE.md.

findings.text: The proof bundle records no driven falsification. proof/VELDO-0011/ contains manifest.json alone; nine of the twelve VELDO bundles in this same commit carry a driven-falsifications.txt AND a per-criterion evidence entry reading 'N of N declared falsification(s) re-driven in this pass and each reddened its own row'. VELDO-0011's five criteria carry one evidence ref each, and it is the same string for all five: 'selftest (PARTIAL, 1 of 34 suites): 104 passed, 0 failed in 0.11s'. So the producer's five passed claims rest on the suite being GREEN, which is the one thing VELDO-0001 exists to say is not proof - a green check is not evidence the check can fail. Compounding it, the runner itself prints 'PARTIAL RUN: no proof manifest, no evidence claim and no landing decision may cite this' on that exact invocation, and the manifest cites it five times (this last part is repo-wide: all twelve manifests do it, and each also carries a separate gate check citing the full green verify). I drove all five falsifications myself and all five land, so the property holds - what is missing is the record.
findings.evidence: ls proof/VELDO-0011/ shows only manifest.json; the per-directory sweep shows HAS for VELDO-0002 through VELDO-0010 and MISSING for VELDO-0001, VELDO-0011, VELDO-0012. python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 18_veldo_0011_release_contract prints 'selftest (PARTIAL, 1 of 34 suites): 104 passed, 0 failed' followed by 'PARTIAL RUN: no proof manifest, no evidence claim and no landing decision may cite this. Only a green `bash scripts/verify.sh` means done.' Comparison of proof/VELDO-0007/0009/0010 manifests shows the re-driven evidence line VELDO-0011 lacks.

findings.text: human_approval: required is declared, unsatisfied and unenforced. I was asked to judge whether the mismatch with .veldo/policy.yaml (standard -> human_approval false) is a defect, and it is not: docs/setup.md:117 defines risk as a 'declared floor; policy may raise it, nothing may lower it', and the only consumer of the field, executor.merge_ready (engine/.veldo/executor.py:257), treats anything other than not_required as MORE conservative. Declaring required at standard risk is therefore a voluntary escalation, and neither the spec's tier nor the policy mapping is wrong. The defect is what nobody did with the declaration. No approval artifact exists for VELDO-0011 (grep -rl VELDO-0011 proof/ returns only its manifest), while VELDO-0012 - the sibling that landed in the same commit and declares the same field, at high risk where the policy DOES demand it - carries proof/VELDO-0012/approval-dmitry.json. Nothing in the gate closes the gap: .veldo/validate.py never cross-checks risk against human_approval, protected_paths is [] so policy_check's approval path never fires, and merge_ready runs only in the reference LiveLoop the gate does not drive. So policy.yaml's merge_rule clause 'every required approval is recorded, unexpired, and bound to this commit' was never tested against this item's own declaration. Either the field should read not_required, matching the tier, or an approval belongs in the bundle.
findings.evidence: cat .veldo/policy.yaml (standard: human_approval false); sed -n '117,124p' docs/setup.md ('declared floor; policy may raise it, nothing may lower it'); sed -n '253,259p' engine/.veldo/executor.py (merge_ready refuses when human_approval != not_required); grep -n 'human_approval' .veldo/validate.py returns nothing; ls proof/*/approval*.json lists VELDO-0007 and VELDO-0012 but not VELDO-0011.

findings.text: AC1 calls validate.parse_yamlish 'the ONE parser the whole repository reads front matter with'. It is not. validate.front_matter (.veldo/validate.py:47-59) is a second, cruder line-oriented front-matter reader and it is the one the repository uses for SPEC front matter in run_all (.veldo/validate.py:846, :853), for spec reads at :97 and :169, for the mirroring read at :646, and by scripts/update_index.py:39 and :104, .veldo/plan.py:37 and :228, .veldo/tracker_mirror.py:446 and :474 and .veldo/executor.py:183. The substantive claim - that this module ships no second YAML reader and receives the parser from its caller - is true and is what the suite actually checks, and it checks it with a substring absence ('def parse_yamlish' not in source, 'import yaml' not in source) that a differently named parser would defeat. The 'one place X happens' sentence is the part that is false about the code.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'front_matter(' over .veldo/*.py and scripts/*.py lists ten call sites of validate.front_matter outside release_contract.py, including .veldo/validate.py:846 and :853 which are the spec loop in run_all. scripts/suites/18_veldo_0011_release_contract.py:236-239 is the assertion, and it tests only the module's own source text.

findings.text: The capability record asserts a binding this item does not build. .veldo/capabilities.yaml:181 says of release_contract_registry: 'a member is bound by the member file's BYTES rather than its front matter, so a plan body rewritten after the binding no longer matches'. There is no binding: member_digest is recomputed on every release_report call, no value is persisted, and nothing compares a recorded digest to a recomputed one - the receipt that would do that is explicitly the next item ('This item ships the digest primitive and the member record that carries it, and writes no receipt'). A reader of capabilities.yaml, which is the machine-readable inventory of what this repository can do, would conclude that editing a member plan's body after a release binds it is DETECTED. It is not detected anywhere yet. The spec's own title carries the same word ('a member is bound by the bytes of its file'), correctly qualified in the body but not in the capability record.
findings.evidence: Read .veldo/capabilities.yaml:181 and .veldo/release_contract.py:285-301 and :632-637; the digest appears only inside the freshly computed member_records of release_report, and grep for member_digest finds no persisted store or comparison anywhere in the tree. Confirmed on live data: release_report over releases/REL-0001 recomputed PLAN-0018's digest at read time with nothing to compare it against.

findings.text: The spec's own decision record now gives a false reason for the name it settled on. The Notes block, 'The draft's D8, naming', reads: 'the module is `.veldo/release_contract.py`, plural and matching the directory'. release_contract is not plural and does not match the directory (releases/). The landing commit renamed releases.py to release_contract.py by mechanical substitution and left the justification behind, and the shipped module's own docstring explicitly REJECTS that justification: 'its name says which of the two it is rather than leaning on a plural somebody has to notice'. So the spec and the source it describes now contradict each other about why the name is what it is - a reader following the spec would look for a plural module.
findings.evidence: git show d449286 -- specs/VELDO-0011-release-contract-and-registry.md shows the substitution '.veldo/releases.py' -> '.veldo/release_contract.py' inside the D8 sentence with 'plural and matching the directory' untouched; .veldo/release_contract.py:15-19 carries the contrary rationale.
